A biomarker's fixed-effects mean at every integration grid point

Source: R/conditionalDesign.R
fixed_mean_grid.Rd

The longitudinal mean \(X(t)\beta\) depends on the event time \(t\) only through the survival-time column and its survival_variable_all transformations. This evaluates it for all rows of data_i (all patients) at all grid points l_i with one model.frame()/model.matrix() call on the rows stacked once per grid point, instead of one call per patient and grid point, whose fixed overhead dominated the run time of the prediction functions. The terms, factor levels and contrasts are those of the fit, as in predict.lme(), so the design matrix is the one the model was fit with, including data-dependent bases such as poly() and splines::ns(). Transformed terms such as log(years) are evaluated at each grid point. Rows are processed in chunks of at most max_rows stacked rows.

Usage

fixed_mean_grid(
  data_i,
  lfit_i,
  xlev_i,
  l_i,
  survival_variable,
  survival_variable_all,
  survival_trans_function,
  fixed_values = list(),
  beta = lfit_i$coefficients$fixed,
  max_rows = 2e+05
)

Arguments

data_i

Prediction rows for the biomarker.

lfit_i

The biomarker's fitted model (terms, contrasts, coefficients$fixed).

xlev_i

Its factor levels, or NULL.

l_i

Grid of event times.

fixed_values

Named list of further columns to set (e.g. the event type).

beta

Fixed effects; by default those of lfit_i.

max_rows

Largest number of stacked rows per chunk.

Value

A nrow(data_i) x length(l_i) matrix; a row with a missing covariate is NA.
